shapes.opening: It's an ordinary chat: nothing big, just talk.
Tease someone a little, good-naturedly: a joke at their expense they can take.
shapes.others: Someone is being teased good-naturedly: play along, tease back or laugh it off.

shapes.opening: Grumble about something that bothers you in the colony or at work.
shapes.others: Someone is grumbling: commiserate, disagree or grumble about something of your own.

shapes.opening: Gossip a little about someone in the colony: what they did or how they've been lately, nothing cruel.
shapes.others: It's gossip: add what you know or think, or say it's none of your business.

shapes.opening: Say something you feel strongly about, where people could disagree.
shapes.others: It's turning into an argument: take the side your character would take; if someone already took it, you may take the other.

shapes.opening: Tell a short story from your past or something that happened to you, a little embellished.
shapes.others: Someone is telling a story: react, doubt it, or top it with one of your own.

shapes.opening: Suggest something the colonists could do together, or something you mean to do.
shapes.others: Someone is making a plan: say what your character thinks of it, add to it or point out a problem.

shapes.opening: Remember something from the colony's past or your own, out loud.
shapes.others: Someone is reminiscing: remember along, or remember it differently.

shapes.opening: Ask the others for advice about something small in your life or work.
shapes.others: Someone asked for advice: give it in your own way, or admit you don't know.

shapes.opening: Say out loud something you wish for, big or small.
shapes.others: Someone shared a wish: say what you make of it, or what you'd wish for.

shapes.opening: Half-share something you've kept to yourself: hint at it, don't tell it all.
shapes.others: Someone hinted at a secret: be curious, tactful or teasing about it.

shapes.opening: Admit something you did or feel that you're a little ashamed of.
shapes.others: Someone admitted something: react as your character would, kindly or not.

texts: Bring the talk to a close with a small decision about it.
Bring the talk to a close with a laugh.
Bring the talk to a close by agreeing to disagree.
Bring the talk to a close by changing your mind a little.
Bring the talk to a close by getting back to work.
